title: Missing a local variable in Jimple representation

title: CallGraph: Add self-loop guard to TargetsOfMethodIterator
problem: Iterating over outgoing call graph edges of a method via TargetsOfMethodIterator can loop infinitely if a self-loop edge exists in the source-method linked list, because the iterator lacks the self-loop guard already added to the other CallGraph iterators. The PR adds that guard.

BODY: Adds a self-loop guard to `TargetsOfMethodIterator.next()` to prevent infinite loops when iterating over outgoing call graph edges for a method.
BODY: calling `edgesOutOf(MethodOrMethodContext)` and iterating the result will loop infinitely
cause: Edge.nextBySrc() walks the same circular linked list pattern (initialized to the edge itself) as the other iterators, so a self-loop makes it return the same edge forever. TargetsOfMethodIterator.next() did not get the guard that PR #2307 added to the other iterators.

BODY: Since `Edge.nextBySrc()` operates on the same circular linked list pattern (initialized to `this` in `Edge.java:223`), it is susceptible to the same self-loop condition.
BODY: However, the same guard was not applied to `TargetsOfMethodIterator.next()` which uses `nextBySrc()`.

title: Fix bug in ClassHierarchy.getLeastCommonSuperClass and imprecision in type inference
problem: ClassHierarchy.getLeastCommonSuperClass can return a class one step too far up the hierarchy when one argument is a subclass of the other. cause: getLeastCommonSuperClass goes one step too far up the hierarchy when one argument is a subclass of the other. The array-merge imprecision arises because type inference does not check whether the underlying array types are equal before merging, so it falls back to java.lang.Object.

title: using HashCodeComparator in class loading may and does cause instabilities
problem: In ClassLoaderImpl.getClassFiles, module entries are inserted into a TreeSet using a hash-code-based comparator that is not consistent with equals. Hash collisions can therefore silently drop module entries, making class loading unstable.
p_evidence:
TITLE: using HashCodeComparator in class loading may and does cause instabilities
BODY: So, using a `HashCodeComparator` in `getClassFiles` may accidentally delete module entries.
cause: TreeSet treats compareTo == 0 as equality, but the HashCodeComparator is not consistent with equals because hash codes can collide. In the Dalvik front-end, DexModuleEntry implements neither hashCode nor equals, so identity hash codes are used, which are unpredictable and are suspected to cause the flakiness.

BODY: The used `HashCodeComparator` is *not* consistent with `equals` as there may be collisions.
BODY: the `DexModuleEntry` class it processes does not implement `hashCode` or `equals`
